scope: Published mathematical models, conjectures, and hypothetical proposals; NONE is a demonstrated time machine.

entries.name: Gödel rotating universe
entries.assumptions: Homogeneous rotating dust cosmology with a negative cosmological constant in its original form.
entries.obstacles: Unlike the observed expanding Universe; no proposed local mechanism to manufacture the global solution.
entries.energy: A classical matter-and-cosmological-constant solution; the central obstacle is global cosmological realism, not simply a generic negative-energy requirement.
entries.claim: The Gödel solution admits closed timelike curves.
entries.next_check: Read the exact metric; reproduce the norm of candidate closed curves and describe its global boundary assumptions.

entries.name: Maximal Kerr extension
entries.assumptions: An analytically extended ideal Kerr vacuum geometry, including interior regions beyond the Cauchy horizon.
entries.obstacles: Inner-horizon instability and questions about whether a maximal analytic extension represents astrophysical collapse.
entries.energy: Vacuum outside the source in the idealized solution; instability and access are the major outstanding issues.
entries.claim: Certain regions of a maximal extension contain CTCs, not demonstrated accessible paths in real black holes.
entries.next_check: Document Cauchy-horizon instability and the assumptions used in analytic continuation.

entries.name: Van Stockum / Tipler cylinder
entries.assumptions: Special rapidly rotating cylindrical matter configurations, including idealizations extending infinitely in length.
entries.obstacles: Infinite extent or severe idealizations, plus unknown assembly and stability.
entries.energy: Not reducible to a simple universal negative-energy claim; depends on the exact model and matter distribution.
entries.claim: A sufficiently rapidly rotating idealized cylinder solution can admit causality violation.
entries.next_check: Compare finite-length limitations with the idealized cylinder solution.

entries.name: Time-shifted traversable wormhole
entries.assumptions: A stable traversable wormhole with two mouths and an engineered relative clock offset.
entries.obstacles: No observed traversable wormholes; maintaining a throat typically requires violations of classical energy conditions, constrained by quantum energy inequalities.
entries.energy: Negative averaged energy and quantum inequality bounds matter for many canonical traversable models; no general engineering recipe.
entries.claim: If an appropriate traversable wormhole were available, a time offset between mouths may allow a CTC under additional assumptions.
entries.next_check: Specify stress-energy assumptions and bound the negative-energy requirements without implying engineering feasibility.

entries.name: Chronology protection conjecture
entries.assumptions: Quantum backreaction and global causal structure may prevent formation of chronology-violating regions.
entries.obstacles: No universal proof across all possible quantum-gravity regimes; specific arguments require specific assumptions.
entries.energy: Divergences or large quantum stress near candidate chronology horizons are model-dependent constraints.
entries.claim: Chronology protection is supported by theoretical arguments but is not a universal settled theorem.
entries.next_check: Build a conditions table separating proven restricted results from broader conjectures.

entries.name: Time-identified Minkowski cylinder
entries.assumptions: Identify events separated by a constant Minkowski translation vector; time-like compactification is imposed by hand.
entries.obstacles: An identification rule does not explain how such topology could be engineered or dynamically produced in our Universe.
entries.energy: No stress-energy calculation or physical topology-change mechanism is supplied in this toy.
entries.claim: Timelike identification gives a closed timelike generator by construction; spacelike identification does not.
entries.next_check: Verify classification numerically and avoid equating the quotient with a physically constructible metric.
